findings.function: all 7 functions (Invariable modifiers, LibBalance, LibTokenSilo inlined)
findings.issue: Single-level mappings are named (stor202[token], stor27[_param1], stor31[idx]) but two-level mappings and mappings inside a struct of a mapping stay raw stor[sha3(...)] with the hash scratch writes kept around them (the P8 count), so germinating amounts and internal balances are hard to recognise.
findings.rule: keccak(k2 . keccak(k1 . S)) is the slot of storS[k1][k2]; keccak(k2 . (keccak(k1 . S) + o)) is storS[k1].field_{256*o}[k2] (a mapping member at slot offset o of a struct stored in mapping S); apply recursively, then drop the mem[0]/mem[32] scratch writes that only fed the hash.

findings.source: LibWell.sol:113 revert("Non-Bean not in Well."); Invariable.sol:40 require(..., "INV: Insufficient token balance"); SiloFacet.sol:173/176 require messages
findings.issue: Every require/revert message built at the free pointer stays a raw memory revert (all 76 P6 lines are this 0x8c379a0 selector with 63 digits); the message text is only visible as hex words.
findings.rule: _x = mem[64] followed by writes of Error(string)'s selector, 32, n and the n-byte text at _x, _x + 4, _x + 36, _x + 68, then 'revert with mem[_x len 4 + 64 + ceil32(n)]' (the length written as _x - mem[64] + c with mem[64] unchanged, i.e. c), is "revert with 'text'"; this needs only _x - mem[64] = 0 when nothing wrote mem[64] in between (writes at _x + k with k >= 4 do not alias mem[64] once mem[64] >= 0x80 is known).

notes: Functions are 900-1,300 lines each; deposit checked in detail (noOutFlow pre-snapshot: getWhitelistedTokens / getSoppableWellLpTokens / getSopTokens / getNonBeanIndex / getTokensOfInterest / getTokenBalances loops; LibTransfer.receiveToken with SafeCast and internal-balance branches; fundsSafu's getTokenEntitlementsAndBalances with the uint128 checked sums, the bean branch and the nested fieldCount loop over stor31[j]; the final checks), the other six by structure; the Invariable part is the same code in all seven ('same as deposit'). Source loops counted are those in this bytecode: LibSilo._mow is an external library function (delegate 0x113cfe45...), so LibFlood.handleRainAndSops' two loops run in the library and are not counted. Loop map: getWhitelistedTokens and getSoppableWellLpTokens -> 'while idx < stor205.length' (field_160 / field_184 filters), getSopTokens -> 'while s < _98', getNonBeanIndex -> rotated 'while address(_153) == stor195: if t + 1 >= _109: revert ...' (P3, 14 copies; the 'if t >= _109: Panic(50)' after each is implied by the loop exit, counted in P11 with the 'min(a, X) <= X' underflow checks of decreaseInternalBalance), getTokensOfInterest's two merge loops, getTokenBalances, noOutFlow / noNetFlow / oneOutFlow / fundsSafu check loops, getTokenEntitlementsAndBalances i and j ('while idx < stor7'), transferDeposits' amounts loop (2161), _transferDeposits (2302), _removeDepositsFromAccount (6418), safeBatchTransferFrom (4181). P7: decode loops of IWell.tokens() and event-data copies. P8 counts the mem[32] hash-scratch writes (each with its mem[0] partner).
summary: Faithful and complete: every in-bytecode source loop is a readable while (getNonBeanIndex rotated). Readability is hurt by raw stor[sha3(...)] for nested mappings with their hash-scratch writes, 76 undecoded require messages, and P2/P4.
